differentiators.name: TRL as a governed object, mapped to eligible Indian schemes
differentiators.statement: Model Technology Readiness Level as a tracked, auditable property of the venture - not a free-text stage label - and map it to the schemes a venture at that level is actually eligible for.
differentiators.why: Every platform tracks 'stage' as prose. A TRL that a return can be filed against is the object both NIRF and IIC actually ask for, and it is the input a scheme-eligibility check needs. Phase 1 found only 32 of 354 DPIIT-recognised startups appear in the NIRF Innovation table.
differentiators.evidence_a: 2 of 40 build TRL natively; 32 of 40 are evidenced-absent. The widest technical gap in the matrix.
differentiators.evidence_u: None. No user in the corpus asked for TRL.
differentiators.contested_note: Inpart builds it for TTOs. IncuMan builds it for HEIs but is in private beta with no customers.
differentiators.falsifier: If two vendors demonstrate a live Indian university running TRL to scheme-mapped eligibility, this closes. Watch IncuMan's beta exit.
differentiators.our_edge: INERTIA. This is exactly the capability that is tedious, unglamorous and requires scheme-by-scheme eligibility maintenance. Incumbents with investor-facing roadmaps will not build it. Phase 5 also shows the budget filter excludes nobody at Rs 1.2L, so nobody is being undercut on price - we would be the only one offering it at all.
differentiators.confidence: HIGH on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

differentiators.name: IPR joined to the venture lifecycle, not bolted beside it
differentiators.statement: One venture record carries the disclosure, the docket, the milestone and the licence. Filing status changes when the venture changes stage, because they are the same object.
differentiators.why: Six of the ten vendors that build IPR are technology-transfer platforms that never touch incubation. The four that do join it are mostly Indian newcomers with no named customer. A TTO officer and an incubation manager today hold two systems and reconcile them by hand - the same reconciliation problem Phase 1 documented for startup counts.
differentiators.evidence_a: 4 of 40 build IPR JOINED to incubation, against 10 that build IPR alone. Only Protrak/IISc has a named Indian university, and it is IP-only.
differentiators.evidence_u: None directly. The FRAGMENTATION complaint category is the nearest signal, and it is about handoffs between people, not modules.
differentiators.contested_note: Protrak (IISc, IP-only), Inpart, IncuMan, ESI. None demonstrates a full venture-to-licence lifecycle in production.
differentiators.falsifier: If IncuMan or ESI ships and names an Indian university running joint incubation + IPR, the joined claim narrows to Protrak's reference advantage alone.
differentiators.our_edge: REFERENCE + SCOPE. StartupHub already competes for the IIC budget line; Protrak competes for the TTO budget line, which is a separate and slower approval chain (Phase 2: 0 of 25 roles have documented budget authority). Winning the IIC budget first and adding IPR second is a sequencing advantage Protrak does not have.
differentiators.confidence: HIGH on absence, MODERATE on demand

differentiators.name: The unincorporated venture as a first-class state
differentiators.statement: Track the idea, the student team and the pre-entity venture as real records with their own lifecycle, which can later convert into an incorporated entity without losing history.
differentiators.why: Every one of 40 vendors assumes a registered entity with a DPIIT number. The Indian university funnel is mostly before that point. Phase 1 shows NIT Calicut attributing 38 of 55 ventures to an undefined 'others' bucket, and 843 ideas arising from 42 activities - a pipeline of unidentified pre-entity work that no incumbent can represent.
differentiators.evidence_a: 0 of 40, with no partial implementations either. Nobody has even attempted the easy version.
differentiators.evidence_u: None. This is a Phase 1 document finding, not a user finding.
differentiators.contested_note: UNCONTESTED. Which usually means nobody thinks it is worth building - and also that nobody has proven it wrong.
differentiators.falsifier: If the Phase 1 'others'-bucket and idea-count findings turn out to be a reporting artefact rather than a real pipeline, this collapses. This is precisely what a Phase 3B interview is designed to test.
differentiators.our_edge: LACK OF INCUMBENT MOTIVE. Incumbents sell to incubators whose revenue comes from accepted cohorts. Counting people who will never be accepted is unmonetisable for them and central to the university's accreditation return. Different buyer, different metric.
differentiators.confidence: HIGH on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

differentiators.name: Faculty and Innovation Ambassadors as first-class entities
differentiators.statement: Model the faculty inventor, the student innovator and the Innovation Ambassador as entities with their own records, so innovation activity is not forced through a 'startup application' form.
differentiators.why: Every incubation platform in the set begins intake at 'startup application'. Faculty appear only in tech-transfer platforms. But Phase 1 shows the institution splits innovation funding three ways - innovation, startup, IPR - and runs 15,000 college Innovation Ambassadors and 25,000 school ambassadors who are not startups at all.
differentiators.evidence_a: 0 incubation platforms hold it (Phase 9 'faculty' flag). NOT MEASURED in the Phase 10 matrix, so the 12 later vendors are unscored on this axis - a known gap.
differentiators.evidence_u: None. Not asked for by anyone in the corpus.
differentiators.contested_note: UNCONTESTED and unmeasured. The weakest evidence base of the six and the one most in need of a Phase 3B interview.
differentiators.falsifier: A single IIC coordinator saying 'we already track that in the annual return' closes it. Do not fund this before that conversation.
differentiators.our_edge: ADJACENCY TO ACCREDITATION. The buyer already produces this data annually for NIRF and ARIIA. It is not a new reporting burden; it is the report they are already late submitting.
differentiators.confidence: MODERATE on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

differentiators.name: Guaranteed migration and adoption - the inertia wedge
differentiators.statement: A scoped, fixed-price migration off forms, spreadsheets and WhatsApp with the data carried over, plus a named onboarding owner for the first two intake cycles.
differentiators.why: Every vendor claims migration; none sells the guarantee. Phase 11 showed the displaced incumbent is free - two Accubate reviewers moved from Google Forms - and identified the real blocker: programmes that have the means to automate still do it by hand, because nobody sells change management.
differentiators.evidence_a: 0 of 40 sell migration as a guaranteed engagement. It is a services offer, and services do not appear on feature pages.
differentiators.evidence_u: STRONGEST user evidence of the six. Three independent routes: the ICUBE institutional record, a six-year university incubator manager, and FRAGMENTATION being the only complaint category with multi-source support.
differentiators.contested_note: UNCONTESTED. Note the trap: this is also the thing the few incumbents most likely to copy, because it is service work and not a feature.
differentiators.falsifier: If the ICUBE record turns out to be an outlier - a sophisticated university that most buyers are unlike - the wedge weakens sharply.
differentiators.our_edge: SEQUENCING. Migration is the only differentiator that generates its own proof: a migrated institution is the reference institution GAP-13 says nobody has. It converts directly into case studies and into the Protrak-style evidence the market currently lacks.
differentiators.confidence: HIGH on demand, HIGH on absence

differentiators.name: Department-level tenancy with departmental P&L
differentiators.statement: Sub-tenancy per academic department, each with its own budget view and correct ownership of IP between the department, the institute and any SPV.
differentiators.why: Multi-campus is table stakes. How Indian universities are actually organised - by department, with separate heads and separate money - is not. It also determines who signs, which matters given that Phase 2 found 0 of 25 roles with documented budget authority: the Department Head may be a cheaper approval than the institute.
differentiators.evidence_a: 0 of 40 demonstrably. Phase 9's 'multisite' flag cannot distinguish campus-level from department-level, so this is asserted rather than counted - a stated limitation.
differentiators.contested_note: UNCONTESTED but unmeasured. Weakest absence evidence of the six.
differentiators.falsifier: If multi-campus tenancy in any incumbent is already department-granular, this is already solved and we are describing a checkbox.
differentiators.our_edge: APPROVAL-PATH OPTIMISATION. Phased differently from the product wedge: this may be worth shipping as tenancy plumbing rather than positioning it as a differentiator.
differentiators.confidence: MODERATE on absence, UNPROVEN on demand

packaging_requirement.name: Deployment shape an Indian university can actually buy
packaging_requirement.reason: Phase 8: Fedena sells a FULL college ERP at Rs 1,00,000 flat with unlimited users - below the recommended Rs 1.2 lakh list. Phase 11 found a second free competitor (Univation, free to universities with Google Ads credit). A flat, unlimited-user, sub-Rs-1.5-lakh shape is the price of admission. Meeting it is not an advantage; failing to meet it is a non-starter.
packaging_requirement.evidence: Phase 8 comparables, Phase 11 RATING/price findings, OQ-03 still unmeasured - so this rests on competitor prices, never on a stated willingness to pay.

gap_scorecard.title: IPR / patent portfolio management
gap_scorecard.note: 10 of 40 build IPR, but 6 of those are dedicated tech-transfer platforms (Wellspring, Helikon, Commercify, SINT.OTRI, KampusCore, KSS) that never touch incubation. The JOINED set is 4. Of those, only Protrak/IISc has a named Indian university - and it is IP-only, which is the reference GAP-13 was narrowed to.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: ESI (ipr=3) and IncuMan (ipr=2) both joined in Phase 11.

gap_scorecard.title: TRL as a first-class, reportable object
gap_scorecard.note: 2 of 40 build TRL natively (Inpart, IncuMan); 5 more partially. Wider than GAP-03 by one vendor and structurally different: it needs no scheme integration to be useful, and it is the object a NIRF or IIC return actually asks for.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: IncuMan arrived with trl=3. Moved from 1 of 28 to 2 of 40.

gap_scorecard.title: YUKTI-NIR / IIC / ARIIA submission workflow
gap_scorecard.note: WAS 'Zero of 29 competitors. Highest-value and most-defensible gap in the category.' Now 3 of 40 - all three Phase 11 discoveries, none with a named customer. IncuMan is private beta; ESI publishes a compliance export carrying a live '(TODO)'; CSM Technologies is a government systems integrator, not a product. Zero partial implementations, which means nobody has solved the easy version either.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: THE MOST IMPORTANT CHANGE IN THE STUDY. Not closed - contested by entrants with no customer proof.

gap_scorecard.title: Unified mandate-spanning reporting
gap_scorecard.note: RETIRED by Rule 1. 28 of 40 vendors build reporting natively or better; exactly 1 has it absent. Reporting is the most saturated capability in the category. It cannot be a differentiator and should not appear in a feature roadmap as one.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Phase 11 found no institutional user complaining about reporting. The spec's own example table proposed 'Reporting -> Automated' as a differentiator; that is wrong.

gap_scorecard.title: Government-grant disbursement ledger traced to a receipt
gap_scorecard.note: 11 of 40 build funding natively and 10 more partially. NestLens Orbit, IncubatX, VentureLink and AcceleratorApp all do grant tracking; ESI and IncuMan both carry a grant pipeline. A plain grant ledger is now table stakes. What is NOT built is tracing a disbursement to a receipt and to the scheme's utilisation format (NIDHI-SSS, DST-TBI, BIRAC) - though Orbit already ships those report formats.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: ESI and IncuMan both added grant pipelines.

gap_scorecard.title: Faculty, Innovation Ambassadors and the non-startup innovator
gap_scorecard.note: NOT MEASURED as a Phase 10 dimension, so no honest count exists. Phase 9 scored 'faculty' as a feature flag: it is held by tech-transfer platforms and by ZERO incubation platforms, all of which build intake from 'startup application'. Phase 1 evidence is strong and independent - 15,000 college Innovation Ambassadors, 25,000 school ambassadors, and institutions splitting innovation funding three ways (innovation / startup / IPR). The 12 vendors added after Phase 9 were NOT scored on this axis, which is a gap in the matrix rather than a fact about them.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Not re-checked. Flagged as an unmeasured axis.

gap_scorecard.title: Mentor logistics at scale - NDA-tiered visibility
gap_scorecard.note: 15 of 40 build mentorship natively, 11 partially - the category's third most saturated capability. The surviving claim is narrow: visibility tiered by NDA plus mentor hours logged against scheme utilisation. incuTrack sells mentor matching as a PAID ADD-ON, which is the clearest signal that the category treats mentorship as an accessory.

gap_scorecard.title: AI that is auditable instead of just advertised
gap_scorecard.note: 9 of 40 build AI natively, 9 partially, 21 absent. Phase 11 is the decisive input: NOT ONE user in the retrieved corpus asked for AI. Phase 11 explicitly listed 'nobody has solved AI-driven incubation' as NOT SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE. The auditable framing survives on VentureLink (logs every score change with actor, value and reason) and on EcoSync's refusal to publish AI scores at all - two opposing proofs that the audit trail, not the model, is the thing worth building.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Downgraded from a feature to a posture.

gap_scorecard.title: Unincorporated pre-incubation state
gap_scorecard.note: 0 of 40, and no vendor even partially attempts it. Every platform assumes a registered entity with a DPIIT number and a cap table. Phase 1 shows why that is wrong for this buyer: NIT Calicut's report attributes 38 of 55 incubated ventures to an undefined 'others' bucket, 94 activities produced 0 IPs, and 843 ideas came from just 42 activities. The university's funnel is overwhelmingly PRE-entity.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Not re-checked. Strongest Phase 1 support of the seven.

gap_scorecard.title: Guaranteed migration off forms/spreadsheets/WhatsApp
gap_scorecard.note: Every vendor CLAIMS migration. Zero sells it as a guaranteed, scoped engagement with the data carried over - which is the only part the buyer cares about. Phase 11 sharpened this into something bigger than a feature: the displaced incumbent is Google Forms and spreadsheets (two Accubate reviewers name Google Forms explicitly), and the real blocker is inertia, which nobody in the category addresses because the people who feel it never go looking for software.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Promoted from a feature to the wedge strategy.

gap_scorecard.title: Departments and multi-campus sub-tenancy
gap_scorecard.note: Multi-site is becoming table stakes (Accubate Enterprise, VentureLink, NestLens Orbit). What is absent is sub-tenancy per DEPARTMENT with a departmental P&L and correct SPV-versus-department IP ownership - which is how Indian universities are actually organised. Phase 9's 'multisite' flag cannot distinguish the two, so this is asserted from Phase 9's narrative rather than counted. A known limitation of the matrix.

gap_scorecard.title: Deployment model an Indian university can actually buy
gap_scorecard.note: Real but not a product differentiator - it is a packaging decision. Phase 8 supplies the proof: Fedena sells a FULL college ERP at Rs 1,00,000 flat with unlimited users, below StartupHub's recommended Rs 1.2 lakh list. Univation offers a directly comparable platform FREE to universities with Google Ads credit. Free is an active price in this market and the entry shape is a requirement, not an advantage.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Unchanged. Phase 11 found a second free competitor.

gap_scorecard.title: A verifiable Indian reference institution
gap_scorecard.note: Protrak/ProrIISe at IISc remains the ONLY named Indian university deployment in 40 vendors - and it is IP management, not incubation. Phase 11 found no Indian university reference for IncuMan, ESI or CSM. EcoSync's TBI-KIET is a vendor claim. The gap survives for INCUBATION, where the reference is the thing a committee actually asks for.
gap_scorecard.phase11_effect: Confirmed against the 4 new vendors; all three have none.

win_strategies.why_it_works: Boring, unglamorous, scheme-maintenance-heavy capability that investor-facing roadmaps will not prioritise.
win_strategies.risk: Requires discipline to stay unfashionable when fundraising gets loud.

win_strategies.why_it_works: Winning the IIC budget line is cheaper and faster than winning the TTO line, so build the module the IIC buyer pays for first.
win_strategies.risk: Phase 2 found 0 of 25 roles with documented budget authority - the IIC line may be easier to reach but not easy to spend.

win_strategies.why_it_works: Every migration produces a named Indian university deployment, which is the one asset GAP-13 says nobody in the category has.
win_strategies.risk: Cannot be bought. Requires selling into institutions that do not currently buy anything.

win_strategies.why_it_works: Offering a cheaper-to-approve buyer than the incumbent's target user converts a budget problem into a procurement win.
win_strategies.risk: A department-level budget is smaller. Does not replace the institute deal.

win_strategies.why_it_works: Capabilities that pay the incubator but not the vendor get systematically skipped. Count pre-entity ventures; they will never be an accepted cohort.
win_strategies.risk: If a vendor's pricing ever moves to per-registered-venture, this closes.

features_map: 9 roles; the research evidences at most 4 as buyers (IIC coordinator, incubation manager, TTO/IP officer, evaluator). Phase 2 mapped 25 roles but found 0 with documented budget authority. Founder, mentor, investor, corporate and resource-provider roles are all DEFERRED.
Feeds differentiator 3 - the venture record must exist before incorporation.
Reasonable, no competitor builds it, but nothing in 11 phases evidences demand and it is a founder-side module, not the institutional buyer.
21 of 40 build incubation natively, 11 partially. Rule 1 applies. Must be built well; cannot be the wedge.
15 of 40 native. Mentorship is even sold as a paid add-on by incuTrack. Only the NDA-tiered visibility half of GAP-07 survives.
Differentiator 2. The full discovery-to-licence workflow is a v2 expansion of the joined-venture record.
Only 3 of 40 build it natively, so the gap is real - but Phase 5 concluded we should NOT compete here: incuTrack and EcoSync are strong and this is most likely a free defensive feature, not a wedge.
Startup-side analytics. 27 of 40 build analytics; market intel is 7 native / 15 partial. Real gap, wrong buyer.
Founder-side. Would require the data this study itself collects. Interesting but not this buyer.
Scheme-eligibility matching is the second half of differentiator 1. A plain grant LIST is saturated (11 of 40 native) - matching is not.
28 of 40 build reporting, 27 analytics. Rule 1 retires this as a differentiator.
Plausible and connected to the TRL object, but Phase 11 found no user asking for risk scoring. Cannot be scoped without interviews.
Phase 11: zero users asked for AI, and 'AI assistant' is exactly the positioning Phase 11 declined to make. Keep as an internal surface over the TRL object, never as a differentiator.
Portfolio view is standard in 15+ vendors.
Cohort and programme management is the most built capability in the category.
Same reasoning as #8 - real gap, wrong strategic choice.
Retained only for the NDA-tiered visibility half (GAP-07).
Second persona for differentiator 2; expand after the venture record ships.
The mandate and accreditation-return surface is the commercial reason the IIC budget exists. Note GAP-03 is now CONTESTED.
Same object as differentiator 1's scheme mapping, seen from the government side.
Two-sided marketplace economics, months of work, zero evidence of demand.
Phase 9 found corporate_match is 5 native / 18 partial - mostly weak. No evidence the university buyer wants this in v1.
This IS the buyer. Research-to-IP-to-startup connection is differentiator 2.
Governance, audit logs and permissions are load-bearing for the accreditation argument and for GAP-08's auditable posture.
Required for the institutional-defensibility wedge; a committee buying a system of record needs to know who certified each record.
Every vendor has email, chat and reminders. Phase 11's one real complaint - email to spam - is a deliverability problem, not a feature gap.
Needed eventually, not differentiating, and heavily commoditised.
As positioning, contradicted by Phase 11. As internal infrastructure, fine - but it must never be the reason a customer buys.
Mentor matching is saturated and unasked-for. Grant/mentor matching tied to TRL is differentiator 1 and IS evidenced. Only the evidenced use ships.

Eight proposed scores, none evidenced. EcoSync's refusal to publish AI scores and VentureLink's actor-reason audit trail are the two data points that matter, and both are about auditability rather than the score.
Requires cross-institution data nobody has shared. Not reachable by a single institution's purchase.
The module taxonomy is sound as architecture. As a delivery plan for v1 it is 12x too large for the evidence. Triaged at module level in MODULES_MAP.

The strongest idea in features.md, and the one Phase 2 independently converged on: the IIC coordinator's question is 'which startup needs intervention', not 'show me the list'. Build the surfaces around that question.
modules_map: Phase 5 said do not compete here
Phase 9: platforms already do this and return nothing to institutions
